messages:
jess (runtime): Heads up — noticed p95/p99 jump on dedicated canaries right after the merge that went out ~1923456700. Dashboards: https://dash.redwood/teams/runtime/canary/dedicated-3 :rotating_light:
omar (perf): saw that too. Quick profiler snapshot points at a kernel-selection path that falls back to the slow scalar kernel for many short-context requests. Flame graph: https://perf.redwood/fg/1923456700
li (sre): CI perf-runner flagged the merge earlier today (perf/unit-latency). I started a bisect and it points to commit 0f3c9a7 (PR #4219) — matches the timing of the canary rollout.
maya (release): PR4219 is the prefetcher + kernel-priority refactor i landed. It changed the kernel hinting order and the eager prefetch cutoff. Diff excerpt: ```diff
- kernel_hint = prioritized_kernels[0]
+ kernel_hint = prioritized_kernels.get(selector, default_slow)
```
jess (runtime): we're seeing a KV-prefetch eviction spike around the same time: logs show repeated "kvcache.eviction=high" during p99 spikes, which increases cache misses and triggers slower kernel path.
deploy-bot: canary deploy dedicated-canary-3 started at 1923456722 (auto).
omar (perf): quick stat: ~78% of tokens in the affected window are served by slow_kernel_v2 rather than fused_kernel_opt. short requests hit metadata path that picks wrong kernel.
li (sre): customer-success flagged a tenant on Dedicated reporting degraded request latency. If this persists we'll be in SLA risk for committed reserved capacity :grimacing:
maya (release): options: hotpatch kernel selector to restore previous hint order OR revert PR4219. Hotpatch is smaller but riskier if we miss other prefetch fixes.
jess (runtime): my vote is pause rollout + revert PR4219 from canary and prod while we triage. Revert is safest to get SLAs back.
maya (release): ok pausing further canary progression now and creating revert PR. tagging @deploy-bot to run rollback.
deploy-bot: rollback initiated for dedicated-canary-3 at 1923456760.
canary-bot: metric-watch: p95 returned to baseline within 30s of rollback. baseline compare: p95 - 120ms -> 58ms. p99 - 420ms -> 95ms.
li (sre): creating incident/esc with CS to notify affected customers. assigning postmortem to "jess (runtime)".
omar (perf): follow-ups: add a regression test that runs the kernel-selection profile on short-context synthetic workloads; add stricter CI perf thresholds for canary windows. Also I'll open a debug branch that isolates prefetch change.
maya (release): thanks, will hold PR4219 until we have tests and a clear kernel-selection rule. After revert I'll ship a smaller PR that only touches prefetch heuristics with a guard flag.
jess (runtime): created revert PR (#4227) and linked perf traces. Will post full traces in the postmortem doc. :thumbsup:
li (sre): closing loop with CS, marking incident high-severity but mitigated.
